bullets.text: Overview of cloud computing's importance and lecture topics.
Definition: delivery of computing services over the internet.
Services include servers, storage, databases, networking, software, AI.
Cloud computing is renting computing resources instead of buying and maintaining them.
Analogy: paying for electricity without owning the power plant.
On-demand self-service: users access resources without human interaction.
Broad network access: services available over the internet from various devices.
Resource pooling: providers share resources across multiple customers securely.
Rapid elasticity: resources scale up or down quickly based on demand.
Measured service: usage is monitored and billed according to resources consumed.
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): fundamental computing resources like virtual machines, storage, networking (e.g., AWS EC2).
Platform as a Service (PaaS): infrastructure plus a development platform with tools and frameworks (e.g., Google App Engine).
Software as a Service (SaaS): ready-to-use applications delivered over the internet (e.g., Gmail, Microsoft 365, Zoom).
Public cloud: services delivered over the internet, shared by multiple organizations, cost-effective.
Private cloud: dedicated to a single organization, offering more control and security.
Hybrid cloud: combines public and private clouds for balanced flexibility and security.
Community cloud: shared by several organizations with common goals or requirements (e.g., healthcare).

sections.heading: Advantages and Challenges of Cloud Computing

bullets.text: Advantages: reduced costs, improved scalability, enhanced flexibility, reliability, and support for innovation.
Challenges: security and privacy concerns due to remote data storage.
Challenges: potential downtime affecting access to critical resources.
Challenges: compliance with industry-specific regulations.
Challenges: vendor lock-in and performance concerns for specific applications.
Data storage and backup (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive).
Business collaboration tools (Slack, Microsoft Teams).
Entertainment streaming platforms (Netflix, Spotify).
Healthcare solutions (electronic medical records, telemedicine).
Education platforms (Coursera, Google Classroom).
Research: large-scale data analysis, machine learning, AI projects.
Cloud computing in AI and Big Data analytics for processing large datasets.
Edge computing: data processed closer to the source to reduce latency.
Future trends: multi-cloud strategies to avoid vendor lock-in.
Future trends: serverless computing for simplified infrastructure management.
Future trends: increased focus on security, compliance, and integration with AI, blockchain, 5G.

Cloud computing is a crucial part of our digital world.
